[tsa-a04-v01] When the concept impresses in order, for entry into the nature just told — then the contemplation-sequence, preceded by true reason, true scripture and the true teacher's instruction, has its use.

[tsa-a04-v10] There, for one pierced by an excessively firm descent of power, true-reason arises by itself through self-attainment — he is called one initiated by the goddesses.

[tsa-a04-v11] For another, by the order of scripture — with elaboration we will say this in the revelation of power-descent.

[tsa-a04-v12] But the task lies in determining the teacher's scripture, and in the arising of the fitting concept that is born of the scripture's chain of kin: that chain of concepts is called true-reason; it is called contemplation as well, since from indistinctness an existing thing is contemplated as non-existent by being made distinct.

[tsa-a04-v13] And here no other yoga-limb is a direct means apart from true-reason, the light-form of pure knowledge: of austerity and the rest, of the restraint-class, of nonviolence and the rest — the yama-type, of retention and the rest, the prāṇāyāma-class — what task is there in consciousness by being established in the knowable merely?

[tsa-a04-v14] Withdrawal too should make the instrument-level excellent; meditation, concentration and samādhi too, performed successively by the order of practice, should impart identity-with-the-meditated-object to the meditator.

[tsa-a04-v15] But practice in the supreme tattva, in the Siva-self, in one's own nature, is simply not possible.

[tsa-a04-v16] For one rooted in consciousness, practice is the form of fixing breath, mind and body — like carrying a load, knowing the scripture's meaning, dancing-practice; but in the form of consciousness nothing is to be taken and nothing removed — how then practice?

[tsa-a04-v17] If it is asked — 'by reasoning too?' — it is said: this is only the mode of removing the residence-in-duality, nothing else at all.

[tsa-a04-v02] For by concept-strength alone beings mistake themselves to be bound; that misapprehension is the cause that obstructs saṃsāra — so the counter-pair concept arises: it tears the saṃsāra-causing concept, and is the cause of prosperity.

[tsa-a04-v03] Such a concept, having crossed all the delimited-natured tattvas from Śiva to the limit, is undelimited-consciousness-merely-formed — that is the supreme truth, the place where thing-ordering stands, the world's essence; by it he breathes the world — that am I, world-crossed, world-self am I.

[tsa-a04-v04] And this does not arise for the māyā-blind, since true-reason and the rest are absent.

[tsa-a04-v05] For Viṣṇu-and-rest are limited in scripture by passion-tattva only, so even in higher vision they show no inclination toward it — therefore they are hostile to true-reason, true scripture and true teacher-instruction alone.

[tsa-a04-v06] As said in the Pārameśvara: all Viṣṇu-and-rest are colored by knowledge-passion.

[tsa-a04-v07] They do not find the supreme tattva, being devoid of omniscient knowledge.

[tsa-a04-v08] Therefore only those pierced by the firm descent of Śāṃbhava-power, having impressed the concept by the order of true scripture and the rest, enter the supreme own-nature.

[tsa-a04-v09] But then would the supreme tattva be of concept-form? Not so: the concept's work is fulfilled merely in breaking the residence-in-duality; the supreme tattva, however, is everywhere all-formed and self-luminous — so there is no service or refutation of it for anyone from concept.

chunks.l2:
[tsa-a04-v18] Even in ordinary practice: the manifesting of the desired form of body and the rest as consciousness-selfhood, and the contemplation of the absence of other forms — that alone is the purpose of practice.

[tsa-a04-v19] But in the supreme tattva nothing at all is to be discarded, it is said.

[tsa-a04-v20] The residence-in-duality too, mark well, is not some separate thing-existing: it is mere own-nature-manifestation — hence the rejection of duality is done by concept, from the saying.

[tsa-a04-v21] This supreme truth, own-nature shining as the form of manifestation, is taken by itself from autonomy; by the order — thrown off, turned toward expansion, then expanding, then expanded — it shines in this way; and the shining too is the Supreme Lord's own nature — so here the yoga-limbs are not the direct means.

[tsa-a04-v22] Reason may favor it, but true-reason alone is the direct means there; it is pure knowledge too, and is impressed in many forms: offering, fire-offering, recitation, vow, yoga. Therein the abode of all states is the Supreme Lord alone — nothing separate exists; for the establishment of conviction in concept, the offering of all states to the Supreme Lord itself is the offering — from heart-nature, the offering in the Supreme Lord is easy for those who themselves show entry into consciousness; hence the external use of flower, satisfaction, scent and the rest was declared.

[tsa-a04-v23] All states are made of the light of the Supreme Lord: for the attainment of the convicted concept, in the light of the Supreme Lord's consciousness-fire, in the desire to swallow all states — the sudden dissolution of all states into the residue of mere light: that is the fire-offering.

[tsa-a04-v24] Likewise, for the arising of the both-natured contemplation, by disregard alone of the states divided by outer, inner and other knowable forms: that supreme tattva is formed of one's own nature — the inner contemplation is the recitation.

[tsa-a04-v25] For the gaining everywhere-always of the impersonal identification with the Supreme Lord, by the identification of equality with the Supreme Lord: the viewing even of the body, even of a pot and the rest, is the vow.

[tsa-a04-v26] As said in the Śrī-Nandiśikhā: all-equality is the supreme vow.

[tsa-a04-v27] Thus, by various concepts formed of portions of pure knowledge, what concept-independent, natural, supreme-truth tattva shines — for establishment in being merely the eternal shining of that kind, the specific concept that tracks its own nature: that is yoga.

[tsa-a04-v28] Therein the Supreme Lord, of the nature of full consciousness — fullness is his power, clan, capability, wave, heart, essence, pulsation, glory; the triad, Kālī, Karṣaṇī, Caṇḍī, Vāṇī, enjoyment, vision, Nityā and the rest — is denoted by the scriptural languages that run according to each sense; by that, by that form, let it be in the hearts of the meditators.

[tsa-a04-v29] And she shines as fullness-consciousness by the seeing of the nature of the whole power.

[tsa-a04-v30] And his powers are countless.

[tsa-a04-v31] Why say more? The world — those are his powers; how can they be taught?

[tsa-a04-v32] In three the world is completed: by which this bears, sees and illumines up to the bearer-limit of Śiva as mere uncaricatured consciousness-form — the Supreme Lord; that is his Śrīparā-power.

[tsa-a04-v33] By which, like a mirror or an elephant and the rest, by difference and undifference — that is his Śrīparāparā-power.

chunks.l2:
[tsa-a04-v34] By which, with the self distinct from one another, by difference alone — that is his Śrīmadaparā-power.

[tsa-a04-v35] By which the threefold holding of this, in the self itself, by embracing, in the form of tracking, grasps — she is the Goddess Śrīparā herself, named by other words such as Śrīmat-mātṛ, sat-bhāva, kāla, karṣiṇī.

[tsa-a04-v36] These four powers, from autonomy, each operates threefold alone.

[tsa-a04-v37] In creation, preservation and dissolution — twelve they become.

[tsa-a04-v38] Thus consciousness first constructs the state within; then outside too by distinctness; taking reddened-nature right there; then, with the intention to reabsorb that state within; then it forms the doubt that is the obstacle to reabsorption, and grasps it; the doubt-grasped portion of the state it constructs in the self by reabsorption; then it constructs even the reabsorber-nature — my-this-form — as its own nature; then, in constructing the reabsorber-nature, the standing of some state by habit-nature, and of some, the residue-of-consciousness-merely; then, by being inseparable from the construction of own-nature, the instrument-wheel; then even the instrument-Lord; then it constructs the māyic knower-form too; it constructs the knower who is contraction-and-release-turned, expansion-grasping, taste-loving; therefore the expanded form too it constructs — thus these twelve Goddess-consciousnesses, directing one knower-object or even several, simultaneously or in order, two-wise, three-wise, even-standing, and arising-portioned, revolving like a wheel, outside too by the order of month, segment and asterism, and within too by the order of pot, cloth and the rest, shining, nourishing the autonomy of the wheel-Lord, denoted by the word Śrīkālī.

[tsa-a04-v39] And construction is motion, throw, knowledge, counting, enjoyment-making, sound, and self-dissolving too.

[tsa-a04-v40] As the Śrībhūtirāja-teachers say: from the throw and from the knowledge, Kālī — by subjection to construction, then.

[tsa-a04-v41] And this meaning is to be considered where it is spread in my composed commentary, in the treatise, hymn and the rest.

[tsa-a04-v42] Not too secret to be shown somewhere, nor to be hidden in every way — so our teachers.

[tsa-a04-v43] Thus what was said — offering, fire-offering and the rest: in this kind the Great-Lord alone is to be thought.

[tsa-a04-v44] All see Viṣṇu-to-Siva as the ground-form only of what is to be rejected, of what is to be accepted; and that false view is necessarily to be abandoned by unsurpassable yogins — for that very reason the knowledge-Lord's great fervor in the hymn of experience: in this kind, in offering and the rest, at the end of yoga, in the fivefold, each many-form establishment; as it becomes, so let him practice — not by discriminating edible and inedible, clean and unclean and the rest, by abandoning thing-qualities, by a fancy-merely-essence tormenting the self. For purity is not the form of a thing like blueness elsewhere, from the command of impurity on it; like the gift's command in initiation — if 'it is impure there' by another command too the same, other-command not-existing from being overridden — if not, the obstructive power of Siva's command alone is established by reason, and established by the omniscient, unsurpassable, endless scripture too — we will say.

[tsa-a04-v45] Therefore from the Vedic on, spoken in the Pārameśvara-system, tantra, clan, Ucchuṣma and other scriptures too, whatever restraint or injunction or prohibition — here it is established as of no effect whatsoever.

[tsa-a04-v46] Likewise it is said in the Śrīpūrva-and-rest, spread — from the Tantrāloka it is to be sought.
